previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by post-bypass hypoglycemia requiring a gastrostomy tube and later bypass reversal was readmitted three days after a norovirus hospitalization for persistent nausea, non-bloody/non-bilious vomiting, watery non-bloody diarrhea, poor oral intake, and dehydration. Evaluation showed stable vital signs and reassuring labs aside from mild AST elevation; given recent confirmed norovirus and no new red flags, stool studies and imaging were not repeated, and bariatric surgery recommended symptomatic management. She was treated with IV fluids, close electrolyte monitoring without need for repletion, scheduled ondansetron with prochlorperazine as needed, avoidance of loperamide due to prior symptom worsening, and gradual diet advancement from clear liquids to soft/regular diet with oral supplements; tube feeds were held to avoid exacerbating diarrhea. Chronic medications for ulcer prophylaxis, pain, mood/anxiety, insomnia, and hyperlipidemia were continued (iron held inpatient due to nausea), and she improved to tolerating oral intake without further vomiting and was discharged home ambulatory with follow-up for nutrition and possible future G-tube removal.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ to presented to the Emergency Department on ___ with new onset nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and ongoing 
abdominal pain.  The patient was placed on bowel rest, given 
intravenous fluids and admitted to the ___ service for 
observation.
Neuro: The patient was alert and oriented throughout 
hospitalization; pain was initially managed with IV morphine and 
then transitioned to oral oxycodone once tolerating a diet. 
Psychiatry was consulted for management with anxiety; see 
consult note for details.  Psychiatry felt that the patient may 
benefit from a clonidine patch, however, this was not continued 
upon discharge as the patient has intermittently low systolic 
blood pressure readings (80-90s).  Ms. ___ will discuss 
further with her outpatient psychiatrist.
CV: The patient remained stable from a cardiovascular 
standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored.
Pulmonary: The patient remained stable from a pulmonary 
standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored. Good pulmonary 
toilet, early ambulation and incentive spirometry were 
encouraged throughout hospitalization. 
GI/GU/FEN: On HD2, the diet was advanced sequentially to a 
Regular diet, which was well tolerated. Patient's intake and 
output were closely monitored; pantoprazole and sucralfate were 
resumed.
ID: The patient's fever curves were closely watched for signs of 
infection, of which there were none.
HEME: The patient's blood counts were closely watched for signs 
of bleeding, of which there were none.
Prophylaxis: The patient received subcutaneous heparin and ___ 
dyne boots were used during this stay and was encouraged to get 
up and ambulate as early as possible.
At the time of discharge, the patient was doing well, afebrile 
and hemodynamically stable.  The patient was tolerating a diet, 
ambulating, voiding without assistance, and pain was well 
controlled.  The patient received discharge teaching and 
follow-up instructions with understanding verbalized and 
agreement with the discharge plan.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital with nausea, vomiting, 
diarrhea and abdominal pain which have since improved.  You were 
given intravenous fluid resuscitation and are tolerating a 
regular diet.  You are now preparing for discharge to home with 
the following instructions:

Please call your doctor or nurse practitioner or return to the 
Emergency Department for any of the following:
*You experience new chest pain, pressure, squeezing or 
tightness.
*New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or wheeze.
*If you are vomiting and cannot keep down fluids or your 
medications.
*You are getting dehydrated due to continued vomiting, diarrhea, 
or other reasons. Signs of dehydration include dry mouth, rapid 
heartbeat, or feeling dizzy or faint when standing.
*You see blood or dark/black material when you vomit or have a 
bowel movement.
*You experience burning when you urinate, have blood in your 
urine, or experience a discharge.
*Your pain in not improving within ___ hours or is not gone 
within 24 hours. Call or return immediately if your pain is 
getting worse or changes location or moving to your chest or 
back.
*You have shaking chills, or fever greater than 101.5 degrees 
Fahrenheit or 38 degrees Celsius.
*Any change in your symptoms, or any new symptoms that concern 
you.

Please resume all regular home medications, unless specifically 
advised not to take a particular medication. Also, please take 
any new medications as prescribed.

Please get plenty of rest, continue to ambulate several times 
per day, and drink adequate amounts of fluids. Avoid lifting 
weights greater than ___ lbs until you follow-up with your 
surgeon.

medications.
